raw_response:
I’m not going to make big changes this year. At my age, with only 8 mu and some people working outside, I have to keep things steady and not gamble. Wheat and maize are still my main support, because if one season is only so-so, the other can still bring cash. Cotton I would keep on a smaller piece, because it spreads risk and sometimes sells better, but it needs more hand work, so I can’t put too much area into it.

For wheat, I will do about like the better households around me: not too little fertilizer, because wheat shows it fast if it is hungry, but not the heavy rate some people use. I have well water, so I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, but not waste pumping money. After wheat harvest, maize must go in quickly, so I won’t do fancy tillage, just hurry and get it planted. Cotton I will keep lighter on fertilizer than wheat-maize and watch insects closely, because cotton can lose money fast if pests get ahead. I need to leave some cash in hand, so everything is a balance between yield and spending.
